To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) it is impossible to design a polylog-competitive algorithm for the general problem in the throughput-competitive model against adaptive adversaries; (2) it is impossible, in general, to design a poly-log-competitive algorithm for a general problem in the online throughput-competitive model; and (3) it is possible to design a poly- log-competitive online algorithm that is throughput-competitive for the general multicast routing problem.

(1) it is impossible to design an online algorithm for the throughput model with competitive ratio better than log n log M, and (2) we present the first online algorithm with polylogarithmic competitive ratio for the multicast routing problem in the throughput cost model.

(a) the throughput model is a useful model for studying online multicast routing and admission problems, (b) there exists a polylog-competitive algorithm for the online multicast routing and acceptance problem and (c) the cost of the edges used in a path is not a good measure for the cost of the path.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of designing online algorithms for routing and scheduling of requests in networks with limited resources.
online algorithms in the throughput framework for multicast routing and resource management.
the design of online routing algorithms for multicasting in networks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have a polylog-competitive algorithm for the general online multicast routing and admission problem in the throughput cost model, and this is the best possible competitive ratio.
we present the first poly-logarithmic competitive algorithm for multicast routing with admission control in the throughput model against an adaptive adversary.
the problem of online multicast routing and admission in the throughput model is hard, but not impossible.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our algorithm is the first to provide a polylog-competitive throughput guarantee for the general multicast routing problem.
we present the first online multicast algorithm that is competitive against an oblivious adversary in the general case, and we show that this is the best possible.
we have shown the first polylogarithmic online routing and admission algorithm for multicast in the throughput model against oblivious adversary.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, by decoupling the routing and admission decisions for different multicast groups, we can obtain competitive results for the general multicast routing problem.
, in the throughput model for multicast routing, it is possible to be competitive even if the algorithm has no prior knowledge of the future.
the online algorithm for the multicast problem can be decoupled into an online routing algorithm, and a separate admission control algorithm.
